## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Higgsfield
Use generate_image, generate_video, and generate_audio as the core tools for image, video, and audio creation. Use generate_3d to turn an image into a 3D GLB mesh. When unsure which generation model fits, call models_explore(action:'recommend') with the user's goal and input context before calling a generate_* tool. For edits to an existing asset, prefer the dedicated tool over re-generating with a model: upscale_image / upscale_video (enhance or increase resolution to 2K/4K), outpaint_image (expand or uncrop an image), reframe (change a video's aspect ratio), remove_background (cutout / transparent background), motion_control (recast / puppeteer / motion transfer). Use virality_predictor when the user asks to predict video virality or analyze engagement, attention, audience response, retention risk, hook strength, or creative performance. Before creating or editing any browser game, call get_game_creation_instructions. When those game instructions require a bundled reference, script, or scaffold file, call get_game_creation_bundle_file. Before building any multi-step, made-to-brief video from a user request — a narrated explainer or story video, an ad / commercial, a UGC / talking-head video, a podcast, and similar templated video workflows — call get_workflow_instructions first (with no argument) to see the catalog of available workflows and their triggers, then call it again with the matching workflow name to load its instructions. New workflows are discovered from the catalog, so always check it rather than assuming which exist. When a loaded workflow requires a bundled template, reference, or script file, call get_workflow_bundle_file. When an Apps UI-capable client user has a local photo/image/video/audio for Higgsfield generation input, immediately call media_upload_widget; do not ask them to attach local media in Claude chat because remote MCP tools cannot read those attachments. For voice creation, use create_voice instead. For voice creation in Apps UI-capable clients, call create_voice immediately when… [truncated]

## Context

`/commit-push-pr` es un comando (de plugin, viene de `commit-commands` del marketplace oficial) que automatiza el flujo completo de **commit → push → pull request** en un solo paso.

## Qué hace

Primero recopila contexto automáticamente:
- `git status` (estado actual)
- `git diff HEAD` (cambios staged y unstaged)
- Rama actual

Luego, en base a esos cambios, ejecuta **en un único mensaje** estas 4 acciones:

1. **Crea una rama nueva** si estás en `main`
2. **Hace un commit** con un mensaje apropiado (generado a partir del diff)
3. **Hace push** de la rama a `origin`
4. **Crea el Pull Request** con `gh pr create`

## Detalles

- Está restringido (`allowed-tools`) solo a comandos de git y `gh pr create` — no puede tocar nada más.
- Está diseñado para hacer todo de golpe, sin pasos intermedios ni conversación.

## Aviso para este repo

En tu proyecto (`claude-code-templates`) ahora mismo estás en `main` con varios cambios sin commitear (dashboard, docs, trending-data, archivos nuevos en `dashboard/src/*/live/`, etc.). Si lanzas `/commit-push-pr` tal cual:
- Crearía una rama nueva (bien, porque estás en main)
- Pero **agruparía TODO** en un solo commit/PR mezclando cosas no relacionadas (los features "live" sin commitear + los cambios de trending data auto-generados)

Si quieres un PR limpio, mejor primero decidir qué archivos entran. ¿Quieres que revisemos los cambios y armemos algo más ordenado, o prefieres usar el comando tal cual?

Ese comando viene del plugin **`commit-commands`**, que ya lo tienes descargado en la caché de marketplaces. Te explico cómo instalarlo/activarlo.

Ya tienes el plugin descargado, pero está **desactivado**. En tu `settings.json` aparece:

```json
"enabledPlugins": {
  "commit-commands@claude-code-plugins": false
}
```

Por eso el comando `/commit-push-pr` no te aparece disponible. Tienes dos formas de activarlo:

## Opción 1 — Comando `/plugin` (recomendado)

Escribe en el prompt:

```
/plugin
```

Se abre el gestor interactivo de plugins. Ahí:
1. Ve a **"Manage plugins"** (o "Browse marketplaces")
2. Busca **`commit-commands`** en el marketplace `claude-code-plugins`
3. Actívalo (Enable/Install)

## Opción 2 — Editar settings manualmente

Cambia el `false` a `true` en `/Users/danipower/.claude/settings.json`:

```json
"enabledPlugins": {
  "commit-commands@claude-code-plugins": true
}
```

Luego reinicia Claude Code para que recargue los plugins.

---

El plugin `commit-commands` normalmente trae varios comandos relacionados (`/commit`, `/commit-push`, `/commit-push-pr`). Una vez activado tendrás los tres disponibles.
